claims.text: Equiatomic FeCrCoNiMn is a high-entropy alloy containing multiple principal elements.
FeCrCoNiMn will exhibit superior tribo-corrosion degradation resistance compared with conventional structural alloys.
The proposed FeCrCoNiMn material is a polycrystalline solid solution.
The intervention introduces Fe, Cr, Co, Ni, and Mn in equal atomic proportions.
The performance prediction applies at 500 °C, a sliding speed of 0.1 m/s, a normal load of 50 N, and in 3.5% NaCl solution.
Introducing multiple principal elements enhances grain-boundary cohesion.
Introducing multiple principal elements increases lattice distortion.
Enhanced grain-boundary cohesion and lattice distortion improve resistance to dislocation glide.
Enhanced grain-boundary cohesion and lattice distortion improve resistance to corrosion-induced cracking.
FeCrCoNiMn will have a 30% lower wear rate than conventional structural alloys.
FeCrCoNiMn will have a 25% lower corrosion current density than conventional structural alloys.
316L stainless steel is an example of the conventional structural-alloy baseline.
The claimed behavior is intended to apply from 400 to 600 °C and at sliding speeds from 0.01 to 1 m/s.
Processing route, microstructural evolution, and environmental conditions may alter grain-boundary cohesion, lattice distortion, and tribo-corrosion performance.
